delivery_identity.procedure: After frozen-source verification, add only documentation/evidence. Preserve original manifests and reports; record a separate input-equivalence and GitHub merge receipt in the evidence bundle.

limitations: The 10 GiB default is a persisted business quota, not a compile-time engine cap. None disables that quota; the fixed 4 KiB SQLite page-number bound is approximately 16 TiB and has not been capacity-tested.
Database quota counts the logical SQLite main file, including metadata and free pages. It does not bound immutable history, original results, WAL, scratch files or bucket allocation.

Cold recovery downloads and validates the complete current database and retained request closure. It needs O(database size) local file space and time; the warm Session then reuses its verified local file with fresh HEAD checks.

The backend is local SeaweedFS 4.51 over real signed HTTP, not AWS Standard. Compute/cache and backend processes were destroyed and restarted, but kernel page cache was not cleared; no power-failure, device-cold-start or cross-AZ claim is made.
64 MiB page cache is a soft target and dirty-page budget is separate. Sampled memory reports, wait4 and shared-cgroup memory remain separately labelled.
The finite historical N0 model uses two result slots. It does not validate v2 production retention sizing, result-byte closure conditions, real SQLite or GiB capacity.
Known object corruption quarantines subsequent HEAD publication in the shared in-process Database handle. It is not a cross-worker durable fence and cannot retract an already-issued CAS.

Warm publication inherits previously verified immutable dependencies; it does not proactively reread every retained old object. No reachable-object deletion or object overwrite is permitted by that proof assumption.
GC is disabled; old chunks and interrupted/conflicting uploads can grow object storage without bound. No production cost, fairness or availability promise follows from these local runs.
